title: Replay sample() filters TASK ids against a CLASS-keyed store and draws <=1 embedding per class

It then draws exactly one embedding per selected class, so a requested replay_batch of 32 yields at most 1-2 samples. self._task_labels (the map that would make this correct) is never consulted.

title: EmbeddingReplayBuffer replay is fundamentally broken: task_ids used as class keys, label_offset=0 collides tasks, wrong head/labels
description: populate() keys the store by raw class label c=int(lbl.item())+label_offset (435) with label_offset=0 at BOTH call sites (1011, 1079), so SHD classes 0-9 OVERWRITE N-MNIST classes 0-9 in the shared _store dict (self._store[c]=... at 443). sample(task_ids) then treats task_ids as store KEYS, not task ids: available=[c for c in task_ids if c in self._store] (449). Call sites pass replay_task_ids=[1] (1050) and [1,2] (1102), so replay draws only class-index 1 (and 2) embeddings from whatever task last wrote those keys, never a task's worth of samples and never N-MNIST (it was overwritten). The sampled labels are the class indices (457) and are fed to forward_from_embeddings(embs, task_name) through the CURRENT task's head (611-615), so replay optimizes the wrong head against wrong labels. _task_labels[c]=task_id (444) records the true task but sample() never consults it. Net effect: 'embedding replay' rehearses one-to-two wrong-task embeddings through the current head, so it cannot prevent forgetting of prior tasks. This is the hub imported by 19 files, so the defect propagates everywhere.
evidence: key c=int(lbl.item())+label_offset (435); self._store[c]=torch.stack(samples) (443); self._task_labels[c]=task_id (444, unused by sample); available=[c for c in task_ids if c in self._store] (449); label_offset=0 (1011,1079); replay_task_ids=[1] (1050), [1,2] (1102); forward_from_embeddings(replay_embs, task_name) (612-614). The CORRECT pattern is present in the same file: RawInputReplayBuffer.sample filters by task_names (498-508).
fix: Key the buffer per task so tasks cannot collide (offset labels by task, or nest by task_id); in sample() select stored classes via _task_labels==requested task_id (mirror RawInputReplayBuffer.sample, 498); replay each sample through its OWN task head with its own labels, not the current task_name. Same defect and the same fix apply to the orphan clone code/m7_trimodal_run.py.

title: Held-out training path is doubly broken: CE reduced before mask, and 6 anchors vs labels 0-9
description: train_correspondence uses ce=nn.CrossEntropyLoss() (default reduction='mean', line 287). In the held-out config, run_one_seed builds corr_ho with num_anchors=6 (line 575) so model.anchors is (6, anchor_dim) and logits_vis/logits_aud have 6 columns (315-316), but the training set from build_paired_feature_dataset contains labels 0-9 (loops range(10), lines 251,261). ce(6-col logits, target=9) raises RuntimeError 'Target out of bounds', so held-out training crashes every seed. Even if it did not crash, the mask is applied AFTER the mean reduction: loss is already a scalar, so loss=loss*mask.float() broadcasts to (B,) and loss.sum()/mask.sum() collapses back to the same scalar, making the held-out exclusion a no-op. main() wraps run_one_seed in try/except (669-672), so the crash is swallowed and NO per-seed CSV rows are ever written; the script's central 'held-out 6-9 retrieval' deliverable never runs. The paper's held-out-retrieval-at-chance numbers cannot have been produced by this code path.
evidence: line 287 ce=nn.CrossEntropyLoss(); lines 318-324 loss_vis=ce(logits_vis,labels); loss=loss_vis+loss_aud; if len(held_out_classes)>0: loss=loss*mask.float(); loss=loss.sum()/(mask.sum().clamp(min=1)); line 575 corr_ho=...num_anchors=6; lines 251,261 build_paired_feature_dataset loops range(10) so labels are 0-9
fix: Filter logits and labels by the keep-mask BEFORE calling ce (or set reduction='none' and average only the kept per-sample losses). The held-out config must train on 0-5 samples only so targets are in [0,5] and match the 6 anchors; masking the data also removes the target-out-of-bounds crash.

title: Held-out-class masking is a no-op: held-out digits are still trained on
description: train_correspondence uses ce = nn.CrossEntropyLoss() with default reduction='mean', so loss_vis/loss_aud/loss are SCALARS (lines 412-414). title: '95% CI' computed as mean +/- 1.96*std - missing /sqrt(n); mislabeled statistic
description: Line 289 prints a '95% CI' as [mean - 1.96*std, mean + 1.96*std]. A 95% CI for the mean is mean +/- 1.96*std/sqrt(n) (normal approx) or mean +/- t_{.975,n-1}*s/sqrt(n). The /sqrt(n) factor is missing, so with n=5 the reported interval is ~sqrt(5)=2.24x too wide and is NOT a CI of the mean - it is roughly a coverage/spread interval for individual observations. Compounding: spinnaker_accs.std() (288) uses numpy default ddof=0 (population std, not sample), and 1.96 (z) is used where t_{.975,4}=2.776 fits n=5. Any number copied from this line into the paper as a '95% CI' would be a mislabeled statistic.
evidence: spinnaker_accs.mean() - 1.96*spinnaker_accs.std()
fix: Compute CI as mean +/- t.ppf(0.975, n-1) * s/sqrt(n) with s = ddof=1 sample std; or relabel the interval as an observed spread. Use ddof=1 for the reported std too.

title: HGRN reset gate is inert: h_prev is always zero, so r*h_prev is 0 and W_r/norm_r get no gradient
description: ImprovedHGRNGate is only ever called with a single argument (self.hgrn(features) at 340, self.hgrn(embs) at 347), so h_prev defaults to zeros on every call and the gate is never used recurrently. With h_prev=0, 'r * h_prev' is identically 0, h_tilde reduces to tanh(norm_h(W_h([x,0]))) and the output is 'z * h_tilde'. The reset gate r (and W_r, norm_r) has zero effect on the output and receives zero gradient, so those parameters stay at init. The multiplicative reset r*h_prev is exactly the operation flagged as the central SpiNNaker risk (R3) and a novelty of the paper - and in the model as run it does nothing.

title: Near-zero forgetting is structural: only hopfield/hgrn/gate are shared across tasks; backbones and heads are grad-isolated

The only parameters shared and trainable across all three tasks are the Hopfield layer, the HGRN gate, and the adaptive gate. Any measured forgetting can only come from drift in those three modules, so near-zero forgetting is largely a consequence of architectural isolation, not of replay. Summaries must not attribute the ~0 pp forgetting to replay preventing catastrophic forgetting.

title: Default forward path silently routes features through proj_shared/proj_private (512->128+384->512), diverging from the documented architecture and from the orphan copy

title: Replay path (forward_from_embeddings) bypasses _split_shared_private, so replayed embeddings hit a different subgraph than live inputs

title: SupCon losses count the anchor itself as a positive (diagonal not masked); the CrossModal comment claiming self contributes zero is wrong
description: SupervisedContrastiveLoss.forward builds mask = eq(labels_i, labels_j) which is True on the diagonal (159), and mean_log_prob = (mask*log_prob).sum(1)/(mask.sum(1)+eps) (164), so each anchor's own similarity is counted in both numerator and denominator of the positive average. Standard SupCon (Khosla et al. 2020) excludes the anchor from its positive set P(i); including it biases the loss toward the trivially-satisfied self term and dilutes the true-positive gradient. This loss is ACTIVE in the default run (scl_weight=0.1, use_scl=True, 608-609). The CrossModal loss only runs under align_cross_modal (default off), but the misleading comment and the shared bug pattern should be fixed.

fix: Mask the diagonal out of the positive set (set self-similarity to -inf before softmax and zero it in pos_mask/pos-count) to match Khosla SupCon; correct or delete the false comment at 201. Numerics-affecting: flag before/after if applied.

description: build_data_loaders materialises every SHD sample into a dense (100,1,1,700) float tensor via list comprehensions over the full datasets (1212-1213) before constructing loaders. It also runs at build time for every invocation regardless of whether SHD is the current task.
evidence: shd_train_data = [_events_to_dense(e,l) for e,l in tqdm(shd_train,...)] (1212); shd_test_data likewise (1213); dense zeros(100,700) per sample (1201-1202).
fix: Wrap SHD in a lazy Dataset that densifies per-item in __getitem__ (or a DiskCachedDataset like N-MNIST) instead of building full in-memory lists, so memory scales with batch size, not dataset size.

title: Timestep count is inconsistent: cfg.time_steps=25 is dead, visual/DVS are cropped to 25 frames, but SHD runs at 100 timesteps
description: cfg.time_steps=25 (52) is never read (PROV-015). The visual and DVS collate fns hard-crop/pad to 25 frames (113-116, 133-140), but SHD is densified to 100 time bins (_events_to_dense time_bins=100, 1201) and shd_collate_fn does no crop/pad (121-123), so SHD tensors reach the model with T=100. Since every backbone loops over T=x.size(1) (275, 353), N-MNIST/DVS run 25 steps while SHD runs 100 — a 4x difference in temporal depth. This makes cfg.time_steps=25 doubly misleading and complicates the mandatory 'accuracy travels with timestep count' reporting, because the per-task timestep cost is not the single documented value.
evidence: shd_collate_fn stacks without crop (121-123); _events_to_dense time_bins=100 (1201); nmnist/dvs cropped to 25 (113-116,133-140); model loops T=x.size(1) (275,353); cfg.time_steps unread (grep).
fix: Make the timestep count explicit and consistent: either drive all collate/densify paths from cfg.time_steps, or document per-modality timestep counts and report accuracy alongside the actual per-task T (25 visual / 100 audio). Remove or wire cfg.time_steps.

title: Output/data paths are CWD-relative ('./ICONS_M7'), so a hub used by 19 callers writes wherever each caller's CWD happens to be

Because this module is imported by 19 files that may run from different directories, results, checkpoints, and datasets can silently land in, or be read from, the wrong place — including the checkpoint-skip trap loading a stale final_*.pt from an unexpected directory.
evidence: base_dir = Path('./ICONS_M7') (1285); data_dir = Path('./ICONS_M7/datasets') (1169); checkpoints under results_dir (1287).
fix: Anchor paths to a stable base (e.g. Path(__file__).resolve().parent or an explicit argument/env var) rather than CWD, or require callers to pass an absolute results/ckpt dir (run_one_seed already accepts results_dir/ckpt_dir — main and build_data_loaders should too).

title: Legacy repo-root package imports resolve only via runtime sys.path hacks plus correct CWD

The name reads as total T1->T3 forgetting, which is actually a separate column total_forgetting_T1_T3 = acc_t1_after - acc_t1_after_t3 (329). title: held-30 whole-number chance level mislabeled (actual 1%, documented 3.33%)
description: The docstring states 'chance 1.0% all-100 / 3.33% held-30', but run_one_model builds number prototypes over ALL present numbers (Pa/ua = number_protos over train+held) and retrieves held-mask queries against that full 100-number pool. Chance for held-30 is therefore 1/100 = 1%, not 1/30 = 3.33%. The verdict threshold wn_held>2.0 is interpreted against the wrong baseline, and the empirical perm null (~1%) contradicts the documented 3.33%.

title: Visual 'spike_rate'/'sparsity' is a post-conv2+ReLU activation rate, not a spike rate
description: _report_spiking_stats treats the stem output as summed spikes, but VisualMapStem.forward returns F.relu(conv2(time-summed LIF spikes)) - conv2 is a non-spiking real-valued refiner, so its tokens are ReLU activations, not spikes. counts=tokens.sum(-1)/T thus reports an activation magnitude mislabeled as spike_rate/sparsity for the visual modality. AudioMapStem returns genuine LIF spikes (s3), so the audio channel is correct; only visual is mislabeled. CLAUDE.md requires accuracy to travel with a genuine spike-rate/sparsity + timestep cost, so a mislabeled cost metric violates the integrity rule.
evidence: VisualMapStem.forward: m = F.relu(self.conv2(acc)); return m.flatten(2).transpose(1,2)  -> not spikes
fix: Measure the visual spike rate at the LIF output (s1 inside VisualMapStem) rather than after conv2/ReLU, or rename the visual column to conv2_activation_rate and stop reporting it as spike_rate/sparsity.

title: Per-digit horizontal jitter is inert for the right digit and boundary-violating for the left
description: Per-digit jitter is far weaker than the boundary comment implies. The RIGHT digit is fully inert: with RIGHT_X0=40 and the min/max clamp, xr==40 for every jitter in [-3,3]. The LEFT digit does jitter but only over xl in {0,1,2,3} (LEFT_X0=0, JITTER=3), spanning cols [3,37); it clips ~3px into the 6px inter-digit buffer (cols 34-39) but never reaches the right region (col>=40). The code's boundary comment is technically violated, but by ~3px, not by a large cross-region slide.
evidence: RIGHT_X0=40 + clamp => xr==40 for all jitter; LEFT_X0=0, JITTER=3 => xl in {0..3}, span [3,37), max 3px into the 6px buffer
fix: Make the augmentation actually jitter both digits within intended bounds (the right digit is pinned; the left moves <=3px); if a buffer-crossing near-miss is intended, widen the left range deliberately and assert it.

title: 'shuffled' negative control is defined inconsistently across phases
description: Phase (a) applies ONE permutation to a single label vector reused for both modalities (lab -> cat([lab,lab,lab,lab])), preserving cross-modal pairing while breaking the label-to-data correspondence. Phase (b) shuffles the AUDIO labels with an INDEPENDENT permutation (lab_a) while visual keeps lab, which breaks the cross-modal pairing itself. The negative control therefore means two different things across the curriculum, muddying its interpretation as a baseline.
evidence: phase a: if shuffle_pairs: lab = lab[torch.randperm(...)]  vs  phase b: lab_a = lab[torch.randperm(...)]
fix: Choose a single shuffle semantics (e.g. permute the cross-modal correspondence, or permute labels-vs-data) and apply it identically in both phases.

title: assert_split_coverage can fail for arbitrary seeds and is then silently swallowed per-seed
description: assert_split_coverage requires all ten digits to appear in pos1 AND pos2 within BOTH the 70-number train set and the 30-number held set. A random 30/70 permutation split does not guarantee full per-position coverage for every seed. On failure the assert raises, and main's broad try/except prints a traceback and drops that seed, so a nominal 3-seed run can silently become fewer seeds.
evidence: assert p1 == set(range(10)), f'{name} missing pos1 digits: ...'  (raised inside run_one_model, caught by main)
fix: Resample the split in make_split until coverage holds (loop), or restrict to seeds verified to satisfy coverage; do not rely on the broad except to hide coverage failures.

title: Module-level pickle-alias hack mutates sys.modules['__main__'] at import time

title: 'Above chance' verdict rests on a binomial z that treats correlated per-sample retrievals as independent

But every query is scored against the same set of prototypes with the same argmax structure, so the trials are strongly correlated (pseudo-replication); the binomial SE is understated and z is inflated. With n in the thousands, an accuracy only slightly above 10% (roughly 13%) already clears z>6, so weak structure reads as 'clearly above chance'. This statistic directly drives the written verdicts about a classifier-leak mechanism and the absence of emergent cross-modal generalization.

fix: Use a test that accounts for correlation across shared prototypes (per-class or per-prototype resampling, or the permutation null with a robust spread) instead of equating sample count with independent trials; at minimum report the effective n and stop treating n_vis_heldout as the trial count.

title: events_to_dense: binary occupancy, redundant max_time guard, and divide-by-zero when all timestamps are equal
description: The dense encoding sets dense[t,c]=1.0, so repeated events at the same (t,c) do not accumulate (occupancy, not count). max_time is guarded by 'if len(events)>0 else 1' but the real risk is max_time==0 (all events at t=0), which makes 'events[t]/max_time' divide by zero and yields invalid indices after astype(int). The guard checks length, not max_time.
evidence: line 142 'max_time = events["t"].max() if len(events) > 0 else 1'; line 143 divides by max_time; line 147 'dense[t, c] = 1.0'
fix: Guard max_time with 'max(events["t"].max(), 1)', and decide deliberately between occupancy and event-count encoding.

title: _events_to_dense divides by max_time which can be zero, producing NaN time indices
description: In _events_to_dense, time_indices = (events['t'] / max_time * (time_bins-1)).astype(int) (1205) where max_time = events['t'].max() (1204). If all events share t=0 (or a single event at t=0), max_time is 0 and the division yields inf/NaN, and astype(int) on NaN is undefined behaviour. The len(events)>0 guard (1203) does not cover the all-zero-timestamp case, and the inner 'if len(events)>0 else 1' (1204) is redundant since it is already inside the len>0 block.
evidence: max_time = events['t'].max() if len(events) > 0 else 1 (1204); time_indices = (events['t'] / max_time * (time_bins - 1)).astype(int) (1205).
fix: Guard with max_time = max(events['t'].max(), 1) (or skip the sample) so the divisor is never zero; drop the redundant inner conditional.
